title: Adversarial network augmentation and tabular data generation for COVID-19 prediction
summary: Augments a COVID-19 patient dataset so classifiers have enough records to train on, then measures the predictions against the real data. GANCT extends CTGAN with customisations for the clinical variables and was trained for 3000 epochs on a V100.
evidence: GANCT extends the CTGAN framework with customizations tailored to COVID-19 data characteristics; GANCT was implemented in TensorFlow and trained for 3000 epochs on an NVIDIA Tesla V100

title: Harmful Algal Blooms Prediction Model: Dealing With Imbalanced Data Using Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Algal bloom events are rare in monitoring records, leaving prediction models trained on badly imbalanced data. CTGAN generates the additional bloom cases and the paper reports an evaluation of what it produced.
evidence: figure 4: evaluation of synthetic data using CTGAN, reporting the generated bloom cases against the original records

title: Synthesizing High-Utility Tabular Data with Enhanced Privacy Via Split-and-Discard Pre-Training
summary: Pre-trains a generator on a split of the data and discards part of it to limit what the released model can memorise, aiming for utility without the privacy cost. The comparison is against CTAB-GAN+ and its variants, which descend from CTGAN rather than being it.
evidence: we evaluate the performance of our models against the popular model CTAB-GAN+ and several variants; CTGAN itself is cited as the lineage rather than run

title: Conditional Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty for Oversampling Imbalanced Data
summary: Builds an oversampler for imbalanced classification and checks that the generated minority samples reproduce the real distributions before using them. The architecture takes CTGAN's conditional generation and mode-specific normalization and swaps in a WGAN-GP loss.
evidence: we propose an oversampling implementation highly inspired by CTGAN's architecture; our approach leverages CTGAN's core architectural principles with WGAN-GP loss

title: A Hybrid Balancing Method for IDS Datasets Using CTGAN and K-Means
summary: Balances an intrusion detection dataset from both directions at once, generating minority records and thinning the majority rather than doing either alone. CTGAN does the oversampling, trained with Adam against generator and discriminator loss, and K-Means does the undersampling.
evidence: section 'Oversampling with CTGAN': we use CTGAN oversampling to create synthetic data for minority classes; the CTGAN training process is optimized using the Adam Optimizer

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Generative Models for Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Student Data
summary: Compares generators for student records on both distributional fidelity and downstream task utility, and finds the two do not track each other. CTGAN and Gaussian Copula are among the synthesizers run, scored with SDMetrics on the OULAD and ASSISTments datasets.
evidence: section '2) CTGAN (Adversarial)'; CTGAN attains the highest SDMetrics fidelity on both datasets, followed by Gaussian Copula, yet not the highest utility
